newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian auto workers reach pact with Chrysler.
newsitem.headline: Canadian auto workers reach pact with Chrysler.

text.p: Canadian Auto Workers union President Buzz Hargrove said on Tuesday the union has reached a tentative agreement with Chrysler Corp.'s Canadian unit, narrowly averting a strike.

"I am pleased to announce that we have a tentative agreement that has just received unanimous approval of the Chrysler bargaining committee for our 1996 negotiations with Chrysler Canada, which will establish the pattern for the auto industry in Canada," he said.

He said he expects union members to ratify the agreement on Sunday, and will announce the second company with which it will negotiate on Monday. The remaining companies are the Canadian subsidiaries of Ford Motor Co. and General Motors Corp.
"We will move very quickly to get ready for the ratification meeting on Sunday at all locations and on Monday morning we will announce the second target for 1996 negotiations," he said.
